newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela calls death penalty barbaric.
newsitem.headline: Mandela calls death penalty barbaric.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela on Monday called the death penalty barbaric and blamed the country's violent crime wave on police and judicial corruption.

Polls have consistently shown overwhelming support among South Africans for bringing back the death penalty to try to combat crime in a country whose major city, Johannesburg, has earned an unenviable reputation as one of the most dangerous in the world.
But Mandela ruled out such a move.
"We don't want to use a method which is considered barbaric," he told the nation in a television interview.
Mandela said the main cause of the crime wave was pervasive corruption left over from the apartheid era and that South Africans should be patient in dealing with the problem.

At times the wave of hijackings, murders and rapes can seem unrelenting. Last week three of South Africa's most wanted criminals -- one sought for at least 16 murders and two Bulgarians who ran a multi-million dollar car theft syndicate -- escaped from police custody.
Gang leader Josiah Rabotapi disappeared two days after he was arrested, while being transported under maximum police security from court back to jail in Pretoria.
Mandela warned such events would continue to plague the nation.
"We must be realistic. These things are going to happen as long as you have corruption in the criminal justice system," Mandela said.

However, Mandela added his government was actively rooting out corruption and had arrested more policemen in the two and a half years of its tenure than the former white-run government did in more than four decades in power.
